name: Ogier the Dane
description: A mythic Danish hero kept by Morgana in Avalon for two hundred years; one of the Sleepers of Oleron may be a powerful faerie version of him.

name: Morgana
description: The faerie who kept Ogier as a lover in Avalon, rejuvenated him with a ring, and later recaptured him.

name: Avalon
description: The faerie realm where Morgana held Ogier the Dane for two hundred years.

name: Crown of Forgetfulness
description: A crown Morgana placed on Ogier's head; dislodging it let him escape Avalon.

name: Ring of the Sleeper
description: A ring worn by the Ogier-like Sleeper; whoever puts it on dies instantly and is replaced by a faerie believing itself to be the wearer's spirit.

name: Sleepers
description: Faeries dwelling in the regio of Oleron, some predating Hermetic colonization, who defend the covenant and can be awakened.

name: Denmark
description: Homeland of Ogier, of interest to Rhineland and Norman magi who see potential to colonize it.

name: Philip II
description: The current King of France, who rules from Paris, built its walls and the Louvre, and won at Bouvines.

name: Oleron
description: A powerful, self-reliant Autumn covenant in a faerie regio that exchanges surplus vis with vassals; liege of Nidi.

name: House Mercere
description: Hermetic House through which Oleron purchases supplementary supplies.

name: House Tytalus
description: Hermetic House that harasses Oleron and is currently embroiled in a civil war; Mnemon of Lapis Crudus is a member.

name: Fudarus
description: Rival covenant of Oleron, presently weakened, that harasses its rivals' outside interests; a client of Anacrôn and home of Harpax.

name: Autumn Covenant
description: A covenant in the mature/declining season of life; Oleron and its rivals are Autumn covenants whose battles focus on weak vassals.

name: Spring Covenant
description: A young covenant in its first season; Atsingani is a small Spring covenant.

name: House Merinita
description: Hermetic House of faerie magi whose members usually see urban spaces as wasteland and follow House Mysteries.

name: House Mysteries
description: Mysteries of a Hermetic House; Merinita magi following theirs become significant faeries.

name: House Bjornaer
description: Hermetic House of shapeshifters with heartbeasts; Micropedus and Luna belong to it.

name: Nidi
description: A small covenant near Bergerac, vassal of Oleron, that hides behind the nobleman Henri and exploits niches in urbanizing land; its name changes with each leader and now means starling.

name: Henri
description: A minor nobleman of Aquitaine who hosts the magi of Nidi in his castle in exchange for extended life; father of Lila.

name: Lila
description: Henri's only child, a daughter whose marriage to a manipulable husband is vital to Nidi's welfare.

name: Bergerac
description: A thriving port barely an hour's walk from Nidi.

name: Regulus of Merinita
description: Magus of Nidi and a Bee King with Strong Faerie Blood, who converts Herbam vis lilac flowers into Animal vis honey and commands bees.

name: Micropedus of Bjornaer
description: Elderly Bjornaer magus of Nidi with a starling heartbeast and Twilight-shrunken feet, originator of the philosophy of covenants exploiting urban niches; an Auram weather magus.

name: Luna of Bjornaer
description: Young Sicilian-born maga of Nidi with a rat heartbeast, originally trained in the Beast Master tradition of Ex Miscellanea; heir-designate of Micropedus.

name: Heartbeast
description: The animal form of a Bjornaer magus, supposed to be wild and noble; Luna's is a rat and Micropedus's a starling.

name: Lilac Grove of Nidi
description: A possibly druidic oak grove in Henri's chase overgrown with perpetually flowering lilacs that yield Herbam vis; Nidi's key vis source.

name: Chase
description: Land reserved for a lord's hunting; Nidi declares its key sites a chase to deter trespass and prevent the Dominion from spreading.

name: Vis
description: Raw magical power harvested from sources and used as currency and tithe among covenants.

name: Aegis of the Hearth
description: Protective ritual; Nidi holds copies of a very impressive version as a hidden resource.

name: Redcap
description: A member of House Mercere serving as messenger; Marcus of Paris is a Redcap majordomo.

name: Strong Faerie Blood
description: Virtue of potent faerie ancestry; Bee Kingship is a variety of it.

name: Bee King
description: Rare faerie-blooded beings, perhaps born when a woman swallows a faerie drone, who command bees, do not appear to age, and die exactly a century after birth.

name: Bee King Virtue
description: A variety of Strong Faerie Blood granting agelessness until death at 100, command and understanding of bees, and immunity to insect stings.

name: Blood of the Bee King
description: Minor Supernatural Virtue for children of Bee Kings: slower aging and the ability to give simple instructions to bees they touch.

name: Beast Master Tradition
description: A tradition within House Ex Miscellanea able to call and command animals; Luna initially trained in it.

name: House Ex Miscellanea
description: Hermetic House of diverse traditions; includes the Beast Master tradition, Atsingani sorcerers, and Anacrôn's lineage.

name: Talisman
description: A magus's personal enchanted item; Luna lacks one and Anacrôn's is a carved human leg bone wand.

name: Mythic Europe
description: The setting in which Bee Kings appear and people like Henri live.

name: Sicily
description: Birthplace of Luna.

name: Twilight Scar
description: A permanent mark left by Wizard's Twilight, such as Micropedus's feathers and shrinking feet or Anacrôn's red shadow.

name: Warping
description: Accumulated mystical distortion from powerful magic and auras, measured as a Warping Score.

name: Final Twilight
description: The ultimate Twilight that ends a magus's existence; Aries succumbed to it and Micropedus expects it.

name: Longevity Ritual
description: Magic that extends life; Henri anticipates a longevity potion and Lapis Crudus magi gain Warping from their rituals.

name: Faerie
description: The realm of faeries, whose forces adapt to the encroaching Dominion and may repossess abandoned spaces.

name: Dominion
description: The Divine realm's presence in human settlements, which Nidi seeks to keep from its sites.

name: Faerie Aura
description: Supernatural aura of the Faerie realm; e.g. weak at Nidi's riverbank, 6 at the Fountain of Fair Waters, 7 at Lapis Crudus.

name: Magic Aura
description: Supernatural aura of the Magic realm; e.g. 2 at the Bridge of St. Cloud and 3 at Bavacum.

name: Divine Aura
description: Aura of the Divine found in some high areas of Paris.

name: Infernal Aura
description: Aura of the Infernal hidden in the seediest parts of Paris.

name: Lacuna
description: A space lacking any Aura, including the Dominion; one lies in the basement of Mathieus's house.

name: Regio
description: A supernatural region layered on the mundane world; Oleron and Lapis Crudus lie within faerie regiones.

name: Atsingani
description: A small mobile Spring covenant, vassal of Montverte, of Brabançon mercenaries in wagons and tents living by brigandage in southern Normandy Tribunal.

name: Atsingani Tradition
description: A Byzantine tradition of wandering sorcerers, seers and healers who once served the Emperor Constantine IX.

name: Montverte
description: Liege covenant of Atsingani, which gifted it a ruined hilltop tower as a council chamber.

name: Aureliana
description: Founding maga of Atsingani from the Byzantine Atsingani tradition, who led her group west from the Theban Tribunal.

name: Viviana of House Ex Miscellanea
description: Filia of Aureliana, spiritual leader of Atsingani, soothsayer and healer who owns a grand faerie wagon.

name: Viviana's Faerie Wagon
description: A grand wagon of faerie origin, larger inside, housing a laboratory and bedchamber and supplying endless clothing and linens with an unnaturally smooth ride.

name: Jacques of House Flambeau
description: Former Brabançon warrior turned Flambeau magus who leads Atsingani's mercenaries and seeks revenge on the Capuchonnes.

name: Baudouin
description: A branded Brabançon criminal in Atsingani's service since youth, reliably violent and chosen for raiding vanguards.

name: Constantine IX
description: Emperor whom the Atsingani seers served in the mid-11th century.

name: Theban Tribunal
description: The Tribunal Aureliana left as the Byzantine Empire declined.

name: Transylvanian Tribunal
description: Tribunal that hounded Aureliana's group out.

name: Rhine Tribunal
description: Tribunal east of Flanders that refused to recognize Atsingani as a covenant.

name: Normandy Tribunal
description: The Hermetic Tribunal covering France, where a covenant may establish itself easily; its customs govern council chambers and vassalage.

name: Roman Tribunal
description: Tribunal with covenants holding chapter houses in Venice, disliked by Mathieus.

name: Lotharingian Tribunal
description: A putative new Tribunal supported by Florum and its vassals.

name: Grand Tribunal
description: The Order-wide Tribunal that sponsored Lapis Crudus in 1064 to heal the Flambeau–Tytalus rift.

name: Byzantine Empire
description: The declining eastern empire from which the Atsingani tradition came.

name: Auvergne
description: Upland region in eastern Aquitaine where Atsingani currently camps and where the Capuchonnes massacred brigands.

name: Aquitaine
description: Region in the south of the Normandy Tribunal where Nidi and Atsingani lie and Brabançons roam.

name: Quaesitores
description: Hermetic investigators who check covenant council rules and prosecute Code breaches, aided by Mathieus.

name: Tourney
description: A Normandy Tribunal contest through which covenants win vis; Lapis Crudus has not participated since its sealing.

name: Brabançons
description: Disaffected mercenary brigands from Brabant, excommunicated by Alexander III, who form Atsingani's soldiery.

name: Capuchonnes
description: A movement begun by Durand in the 1180s to eradicate brigands, which massacred 3000 in Auvergne then became brigands themselves.

name: Durand
description: A freeman who founded the Capuchonnes in the 1180s.

name: Brabant
description: Duchy east of Flanders from which the Brabançons originate.

name: Pope Alexander III
description: Pope who in 1179 banned freebooting soldiers alongside heretics, naming the Brabanters.

name: Henry II of England
description: Plantagenet king whose son rebelled against him; married Eleanor of Aquitaine.

name: Henry the Young King
description: Son of Henry II, called Henry, who warred on his father but could not pay his Brabançons.

name: Noialle
description: Town massacred and plundered by Brabançons on the way to Limoges.

name: Limoges
description: Town in Aquitaine toward which the Brabançons marched.

name: Le Puy
description: Town from which the Capuchonnes spread.

name: Branded Criminal
description: Flaw of bearing a criminal brand; Baudouin's marks his face.

name: Puissant Bows
description: Virtue boosting the Bows ability; held by Baudouin.

name: Tough
description: Virtue granting extra Soak; held by Baudouin.

name: Weakness
description: Personality Flaw; Baudouin's is loose women.

name: Depressed
description: Personality Flaw held by Baudouin.

name: Animal Handling
description: Ability to handle animals; Baudouin specializes in horses.

name: Aquitaine Lore
description: Area lore of Aquitaine.

name: Athletics
description: Physical ability.

name: Awareness
description: Ability to notice things.

name: Brawl
description: Unarmed and dagger combat ability.

name: Bows
description: Martial ability with bows; Baudouin favors the crossbow.

name: Carouse
description: Ability at drinking and gambling.

name: Concentration
description: Ability to maintain focus.

name: French
description: Language ability.

name: Hunt
description: Hunting ability.

name: Profession: Carpenter
description: Carpentry profession ability.

name: Ride
description: Riding ability.

name: Single Weapon
description: Martial ability with a single weapon.

name: Stealth
description: Ability to move unseen.

name: Survival
description: Wilderness survival ability.

name: Ile de France
description: The rich central region of the Normandy Tribunal and seat of French royal power, including Paris.

name: Capetian Dynasty
description: The royal Capetian house of France, whose historical domain is the Ile de France.

name: Hugh Capet
description: Elected king in 987 at Senlis, making Paris his capital.

name: Senlis
description: Town where Hugh Capet was elected king.

name: Merovingian Kings
description: Early Frankish kings who donated lands to the Church and whose locks granted mystical powers.

name: Paris
description: The greatest city in northern Europe and seat of the French monarchy, a royal, scholarly and commercial center with Divine and Infernal auras.

name: Île de la Cité
description: The mile-long central island of Paris, its ecclesiastical and administrative core.

name: Left Bank of Paris
description: The intellectual and scholarly district of Paris, center of Roman Lutetia.

name: Right Bank of Paris
description: The largest, commercial district of Paris, also called Le Marais.

name: Notre-Dame de Paris
description: Giant cathedral in the new French style on the Île de la Cité, begun 1163.

name: Louvre
description: Monolithic fortress of Philip II erected in 1190 west of Paris, housing his residence, treasury and arsenal.

name: Petit Pont
description: Short stone bridge of 1186 connecting the Île de la Cité to the left bank.

name: Les Halles
description: The great central market of Paris, covered by Philip II in 1183.

name: Hanse Parisienne
description: The principal league of merchants in Paris.

name: Montmartre
description: Hill north of Paris named for the martyrdom of St. Denis, formerly Mons Mercurius.

name: Lutetia
description: Roman town that preceded Paris, centered on the left bank.

name: Parisii
description: A fishing tribe who first settled the island in the Seine, giving Paris its name.

name: Brethren of the Free Spirit
description: A large heretical cult in Paris whose members consider themselves immune to sin.

name: Peter Abélard
description: Controversial philosopher and theologian who tutored and secretly wed Héloïse, was castrated, and later became a monk.

name: Héloïse
description: Niece of Fulbert who loved and wed Abélard, then became a nun.

name: Fulbert
description: Canon of Paris, uncle of Héloïse, who had Abélard castrated.

name: Astralabe
description: Son of Abélard and Héloïse.

name: Argenteuil
description: Nunnery near Paris to which Héloïse moved.

name: St-Gildas-de-Rhuys
description: Monastery on the Gulf of Morbihan where Abélard retreated.

name: St. Gildas
description: Founder in the 6th century of St-Gildas-de-Rhuys.

name: Cluny
description: Monastery where Abélard ended his life as a monk.

name: Knights Templar
description: Holy order whose Paris treasury acts as a bank, lending and transferring money.

name: Templar Treasury
description: The fabulously wealthy Templar temple in Paris operating as an early bank.

name: Jerusalem
description: Site of a large Templar bank where pilgrims withdraw funds.

name: Attila the Hun
description: Hun leader who threatened Paris in 451 and besieged Orléans.

name: St. Geneviève
description: Peasant girl whose prayers saved Paris from Attila; patron saint of Paris.

name: Childeric
description: Frankish king whose siege of Paris Geneviève thwarted.

name: Clovis
description: First Christian Frankish king, founder of St. Peter and St. Paul, who took the Oriflamme.

name: Odo, Count of Paris
description: Led the defense of Paris against the Vikings in 885.

name: Vikings
description: Raiders who sacked Paris in 845 and later became Normans.

name: Abbey Church of St. Geneviève
description: Abbey church on a hill on the left bank of Paris.

name: Abbey Church of St. Germanus
description: Left-bank abbey church, burial place of most Merovingian kings.

name: King of the Beggars
description: Title of the ruler of the Parisian beggars and thieves, also the Grand Coësre; currently held by Anacrôn.

name: Argotiers
description: The beggars working for the King of the Beggars, licensed to beg in specific ways and speaking an argot.

name: Cagoux
description: Master-thieves who enforce the King of the Beggars' edicts as his chief nobles.

name: Archisuppôts
description: Arch-thieves, usually from the dregs of the clergy, who teach the king's law and train apprentice beggars.

name: Marcandiers
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who pretend to be robbed merchants.

name: Francs-mitoux
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who feign fainting fits in public.

name: Malingreux
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who fake a dreadful disease with fat and ashes.

name: Piètres
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who feign lameness on crutches.

name: Sabouleux
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who daub themselves with blood and froth with soap.

name: Polissons
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who go naked begging for clothes.

name: Courtauds-de-boutanche
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who pretend to be out-of-work tradesmen.

name: Hutins
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who pretend to be bitten by mad dogs.

name: Coquillards
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who carry forged pilgrim certificates.

name: Calots
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who sit slack-jawed as apparent dotards.

name: Capons
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who cheat marks at cards.

name: Narquois
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who are pensioned soldiers extorting with threats.

name: Millards
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who racketeer among peasants in the countryside.

name: Orphelines
description: A court of Parisian argotiers who slit the purses of the rich.

name: Anacrôn
description: Eremite magus of House Ex Miscellanea and legless King of the Beggars of Paris, whose lineage's magic is founded on pain and infirmity.

name: Anacrôn's Talisman
description: A wand carved from a human leg bone inlaid with bloodstones, enchanted with Agony of the Uncharitable Stranger and Hobble the Foul-Mouthed Wretch.

name: Affreux
description: A brindled mastiff, Anacrôn's familiar, able to create a ward repelling people and grow to bear size.

name: Boiteux
description: Mastiff son of Affreux and Anacrôn's Magical Animal Companion; pulls his trolley.

name: Familiar
description: A magus's bonded magical animal; Affreux is Anacrôn's.

name: Harpax
description: Magus of Fudarus who declared Wizard's War on Anacrôn's accuser.

name: Wizard's War
description: Hermetic sanctioned conflict between magi; Harpax's declaration prevented charges against Anacrôn.

name: High Crimes
description: Serious breaches of the Code investigated by the Quaesitores.

name: Mystery Cult
description: Secret Hermetic cults that might ally with Anacrôn.

name: Decrepitude
description: Aging-related decline riddling Anacrôn's ancient ancestors.

name: Interfering with Mundanes
description: Hermetic crime of which Anacrôn has twice been accused.

name: The Gift
description: The Virtue enabling Hermetic magic; rare, and some Parisians have it undiscovered.

name: Hermetic Magus
description: Social Status Virtue of being a Hermetic magus.

name: Death Prophecy
description: House Virtue of Anacrôn's lineage: one can only be killed when he is the eldest of his tradition alive.

name: Life-Linked Spontaneous Magic
description: Virtue held by Anacrôn.

name: Affinity with Corpus
description: Virtue improving Corpus; held by Anacrôn.

name: Minor Magical Focus
description: Virtue; Anacrôn's focus is infirmity.

name: Personal Vis Source
description: House Virtue; Anacrôn's is the skin he scrapes from his leg-stumps, yielding Corpus vis.

name: Piercing Gaze
description: Virtue held by Anacrôn.

name: Puissant Leadership
description: Virtue boosting Leadership; held by Anacrôn.

name: Quiet Magic
description: Virtue held by Anacrôn.

name: Social Contacts
description: Virtue held by Anacrôn.

name: Crippled
description: Flaw held by the legless Anacrôn.

name: Envious
description: Personality Flaw held by Anacrôn.

name: Painful Magic
description: House Flaw of Anacrôn's lineage, whose magic is founded on pain.

name: Deficient Form
description: Flaw; Anacrôn's is Imaginem.

name: Infamous
description: Flaw held by Anacrôn.

name: Magical Animal Companion
description: Listed among Anacrôn's Flaws; his is the mastiff Boiteux.

name: Argot
description: Language of the Parisian beggars.

name: Argotiers Lore
description: Knowledge of the argotiers.

name: Artes Liberales
description: Academic ability; used to predict Bavacum's active road.

name: Chirurgy
description: Medical ability.

name: Civil and Canon Law
description: Legal ability.

name: Code of Hermes (Ability)
description: Knowledge of Hermetic law.

name: Finesse
description: Ability for precise spellcasting.

name: Folk Ken
description: Ability to understand people.

name: Guile
description: Ability to deceive.

name: Ile de France Lore
description: Area lore of the Ile de France.

name: Intrigue
description: Ability at politics and scheming.

name: Kingdom of France Lore
description: Area lore of France.

name: Latin
description: Language of scholars and magi.

name: Leadership
description: Ability to command.

name: Legerdemain
description: Sleight of hand ability.

name: Magic Theory
description: Hermetic theoretical ability.

name: Paris Lore
description: Area lore of Paris.

name: Parma Magica
description: The Hermetic magical defense ability.

name: Penetration
description: Ability to overcome magic resistance.

name: Order of Hermes Lore
description: Knowledge of the Order.

name: Creo
description: Hermetic Technique; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Intellego
description: Hermetic Technique; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Muto
description: Hermetic Technique; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Perdo
description: Hermetic Technique; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Rego
description: Hermetic Technique; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Animal
description: Hermetic Form; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Aquam
description: Hermetic Form; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Auram
description: Hermetic Form; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Corpus
description: Hermetic Form; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Herbam
description: Hermetic Form; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Ignem
description: Hermetic Form; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Imaginem
description: Hermetic Form; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Mentem
description: Hermetic Form; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Terram
description: Hermetic Form; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Vim
description: Hermetic Form; listed among Anacrôn's Arts.

name: Agony of the Uncharitable Stranger
description: PeCo 30 talisman enchantment riddling the target with stabbing pains.

name: Hobble the Foul-Mouthed Wretch
description: PeCo 40 talisman enchantment laming the target for a Sun duration.

name: Agony of the Beast
description: PeAn 15 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Arm of the Infant
description: MuCo 20 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Aura of Rightful Authority
description: ReMe 20 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Bane of the Decrepit Body
description: PeCo 25 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Circle of Beast Warding
description: ReCo 5 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Cripple the Howling Wolf
description: PeAn 25 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Disguise of the New Visage
description: MuCo 15 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Gift of Frog's Legs
description: ReCo 15 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Loss of But a Moment's Memory
description: PeMe 15 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Panic of the Trembling Heart
description: CrMe 15 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Posing the Silent Question
description: InMe 20 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Prison of Flames
description: MuIg 20 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Stench of Twenty Corpses
description: CrAu 10 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: The Irresistible Pressgang
description: CrMe Ritual granting a group fanatical loyalty to the caster for a year and 5 Warping Points; Anacrôn uses it to make cagoux.

name: The Twisted Spine
description: Mu(Pe)Co 20 spell crippling the target as his backbone warps and twists.

name: The Wound that Weeps
description: PeCo 15 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Trust of Childlike Faith
description: PeMe 10 spell known by Anacrôn.

name: Eboris
description: A small neutral covenant in Paris, the House of the Ivory Carvers, led by Mathieus, hosting young Jerbiton magi and the Itinerarium rather than research.

name: Mathieus of Constantinople
description: Archmagus follower of Jerbiton who fled the sack of Constantinople, leads Eboris, and is the Warden of Paris.

name: Maria of Constantinople
description: Mater of Mathieus.

name: Constantinople
description: The new Rome, sacked by crusaders in 1204, where Mathieus's covenant was destroyed.

name: Valnastium
description: Covenant with a library Mathieus was consulting; a stop on the Itinerarium.

name: Latin Empire
description: The crusader state in former Byzantine lands that Mathieus wished to leave.

name: Marseilles
description: Port to which Mathieus sailed after Constantinople fell.

name: House Jerbiton
description: Hermetic House of culture that sends apprentices to cities; its Primus draws Mathieus into its affairs.

name: Primus
description: Head of a Hermetic House; the Jerbiton Primus is Andru.

name: Andru
description: The Jerbiton Primus, who trained Constantina and would investigate threats from Asia.

name: Constantina filia Andru of Jerbiton
description: Young firebrand trained by the Primus, currently Mathieus's designated heir.

name: Itinerarium
description: A great tour of artistic cities acculturating Jerbiton apprentices, travelling from Paris through the Alps to Valnastium and Italy.

name: Antigones
description: The rising generation of Jerbiton magi, supported by Mathieus, who evangelize antigonic philosophy.

name: Sweated Shillings
description: The shifting gaggle of young magi living with Mathieus, named after clipped coins.

name: Rue de la Tabletterie
description: Paris street where Mathieus's house, an ivory-carving business, stands.

name: Warden of Paris
description: Mathieus's role, recognized by House Jerbiton, as dedicated preserver of Paris.

name: Code of Hermes
description: The law of the Order of Hermes; injured sodales make undesired activity a breach.

name: Hoplite
description: Hermetic enforcer of the Code; Mathieus is not one.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of Hermetic magi.

name: Certamen
description: Hermetic magical duel; further study would improve Mathieus's performance.

name: Marcus of Paris
description: Redcap majordomo of Mathieus who sells intelligence about Paris and recruits servants for covenants.

name: Venice
description: City Mathieus loathes and blames for the Fourth Crusade; Roman Tribunal covenants have chapter houses there.

name: Fourth Crusade
description: The 1204 crusade that sacked Constantinople and made Baldwin IX emperor.

name: Trebizond
description: Tiny kingdom at the edge of the Hermetic world through which ivory enters Europe.

name: Huns
description: Invaders from Asia whose last coming was presaged by trade disruption.

name: Hedge Wizard
description: Non-Hermetic urban magicians, including Gifted Parisians the Order must police.

name: St. Denis
description: Martyr and patron saint of France, buried at the abbey bearing his name.

name: Basilica of St. Denis
description: Royal abbey church north of Paris, the first in the new French style, housing royal tombs and the Oriflamme.

name: St. Denis (town)
description: Wealthy royal town north of Paris hosting the Lendit fair.

name: Dagobert I
description: Founder of the monastery of St. Denis in the 7th century.

name: Pepin the Short
description: Expanded the monastery of St. Denis.

name: Abbot Suger
description: Abbot of St. Denis, regent for Louis VII, who built the basilica after a vision of the heavenly Bethlehem.

name: Louis VII
description: King of France and friend of Suger who went on the Second Crusade.

name: Childebert
description: Son of Clovis buried at St. Denis.

name: Lendit Fair
description: Annual October fair near St. Denis specializing in parchment.

name: St. Cloud
description: Town on the Seine named after Clodoald, now belonging to the bishops of Paris.

name: Clodoald
description: Grandson of Clovis who cut his hair, founded a monastery and gave St. Cloud its name.

name: Clodomir
description: Son of Clovis, father of Clodoald, and king of Burgundy at Orléans.

name: Bridge of St. Cloud
description: Old wooden bridge with a Magic aura of 2; any king who sets foot on it is said to die.

name: Oriflamme
description: The flame-colored royal standard of France kept at St. Denis, which bolsters the king's troops and overrides other supernatural effects.

name: Syragius
description: Roman king from whom Clovis took the Oriflamme at Soissons.

name: Charlemagne
description: Emperor who possessed the Oriflamme and gave the Sainte-Chemise to Chartres.

name: Battle of Bouvines
description: 1214 battle where Philip won and captured Count Ferdinand of Flanders.

name: Ferdinand of Flanders
description: Count of Flanders captured at Bouvines, held for ransom in Paris; husband of Joan.

name: Chartres
description: City on the Eure with an ancient sacred well, cathedral, and the Sainte-Chemise relic.

name: Cathedral of Chartres
description: Cathedral rebuilt after the 1194 fire, with a new French-style nave finished in 1220.

name: Sainte-Chemise
description: The tunic worn by the Virgin Mary at Christ's birth, relic of Chartres that miraculously survived the 1194 fire.

name: Virgin Mary
description: Saint venerated at Chartres.

name: Carnutes
description: Ancient Gaulish tribe giving Chartres its name, home near Orléans.

name: Seine
description: Great river flowing through Paris.

name: Loire
description: Great river flowing through the Ile de France toward Anjou.

name: Forest of Cuise
description: Great forest on the northeastern edge of the Ile de France.

name: Forest of Yvelines
description: Forest south of Paris.

name: Forest of Fontainebleau
description: Rocky forest south of Paris with druidic groves, a Faerie regio, and the covenant of Lapis Crudus.

name: Sologne
description: Marshy heathland forest south of Orléans.

name: Fountain of Fair Waters
description: Spring at the center of a Faerie regio (aura 6) in Fontainebleau, home of a nymph and white stag.

name: Nymph of Fontaine-Belle-Eau
description: A beautiful nymph, believed an embodiment of Diana, who curses persistent hunters.

name: White Stag of Fontainebleau
description: A placid white stag accompanying the nymph.

name: Lapis Crudus
description: Once-great covenant founded 1064 to heal the Flambeau–Tytalus rift, trapped in a faerie regio in Fontainebleau for eighty years by Candidus.

name: Caput Capra
description: A ruined, abandoned or lost covenant of the Ile de France.

name: Candidus
description: A powerful chalk-white eyeless faerie of Fontainebleau who grants wishes through bargains and trapped Lapis Crudus.

name: Aries of House Flambeau
description: Lapis Crudus magus who tricked Candidus into protecting the covenant; succumbed to Final Twilight five years ago.

name: House Flambeau
description: Hermetic House whose rift with Tytalus Lapis Crudus was founded to heal.

name: House Bonisagus
description: Hermetic House; one Bonisagus of Trianoma's line helped found Lapis Crudus.

name: Trianoma
description: Founder whose line of Bonisagus contributed a founder of Lapis Crudus.

name: Schism War
description: Hermetic war after which Lapis Crudus was founded; Florum avoided it.

name: Les Trois Pignons
description: Barren sandstone massif in western Fontainebleau housing Lapis Crudus.

name: Mirror of Lapis Crudus
description: A magical mirror in a hut straddling the regio boundary, created by Mnemon; now the gate through which persons of like status swap places.

name: Bleeding Stone
description: Stone in a cavern below Lapis Crudus's council chamber, source of its name and of Corpus and Terram vis.

name: Somnifer of Merinita
description: Dream-magic master of Lapis Crudus who scried the outside world through dreams and trained an apprentice through the mirror.

name: Mnemon of Tytalus
description: Rego master of Lapis Crudus who created the mirror gate and renegotiated with Candidus.

name: Languidus
description: Somnifer's filius, representing Lapis Crudus at Tribunal without formal membership.

name: Oath of Fealty
description: The oath binding vassal covenants to a liege in the Normandy Tribunal.

name: Sens
description: City and archbishopric overseeing most bishoprics of the Ile de France.

name: Cathedral of St. Étienne
description: Second-earliest church in the new French style, in Sens.

name: William of Sens
description: Architect who worked on Canterbury Cathedral.

name: St. Thomas Becket
description: Saint whose alb is kept at Sens.

name: Senones
description: Gaulish tribe giving Sens its name.

name: Orléans
description: City on the Loire, once Merovingian capital of Burgundy, famed for its cathedral school.

name: Theodulf
description: Goth poet-scholar, bishop of Orléans, who founded Fleury's monastic school.

name: Pope Honorius III
description: Pope who in 1219 banned teaching law in Paris.

name: Fleury
description: Abbey on the Loire at a former druidic assembly grove, resting place of St. Benedict.

name: St. Benedict
description: Founder of western monasticism whose relics rest at Fleury.

name: Basilica of St. Benedict
description: White-stone basilica at Fleury finished in 1218.

name: Monte Cassino
description: Italian monastery from which St. Benedict's remains were moved.

name: Abbo
description: Scholar abbot of Fleury, confidante of Robert II, who expanded its library.

name: Robert II
description: French king whose confidante was Abbo.

name: History of the Franks (Aimon)
description: Tome by the monk Aimon, official chronicle of the Capetians; summae on French Royalty, Ile de France, and Divine Lore.

name: Aimon
description: Monk of Fleury who wrote the History of the Franks.

name: Gregory of Tours
description: Author of the more famous ancient History of the Franks.

name: Bourges
description: Heavily fortified royal city south of the Loire and seat of an archbishopric.

name: Great Tower of Bourges
description: Keep in Bourges's southern wall, prototype of the Louvre.

name: Cathedral of Bourges
description: Half-built French-style cathedral begun 1195.

name: Philip I
description: French king who bought Bourges in 1100.

name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
description: Wife of Henry II Plantagenet.

name: Henry III of England
description: English king and duke of Aquitaine.

name: Henry de Sully
description: Archbishop who began Bourges cathedral.

name: William de Donjon
description: Archbishop of Bourges, canonised 1218, drawing pilgrims.

name: Flanders
description: Densely populated industrial province of the Normandy Tribunal famed for woollen cloth.

name: Picardy
description: Rural northern realm south of Flanders with Carolingian cities.

name: Boulonnais Coast
description: Tame wilderness of interest to magi.

name: Somme
description: River valley of interest to magi.

name: Montagne de Reims
description: Wilderness of interest to magi.

name: Baldwin Ironarm
description: First Count of Flanders (866) who built Bruges's castle.

name: Charles the Bald
description: Father-in-law of Baldwin Ironarm.

name: Wateringues
description: Societies of landowners reclaiming Flemish marshland.

name: Lille
description: Seat of the Counts of Flanders and a cloth fair town.

name: Douai
description: City with a great keep of the Counts of Flanders.

name: Joan of Hainault
description: Ruler of Flanders since 1205, niece of Philip II.

name: Baldwin IX
description: Count of Flanders elected Emperor of Constantinople in 1204.

name: Bruges
description: Flanders' greatest port, linked to Damme by canal after the 1134 tidal wave.

name: Robert the Frisian
description: Made Bruges his capital in 1093.

name: Zwin
description: Estuary opened by the 1134 tidal wave.

name: Damme
description: Harbor for Bruges.

name: Church of St. Donatius
description: Bruges's largest church.

name: Basilica of the Holy Blood
description: Bruges church housing a reliquary of the Blood of Christ.

name: Relic of the Holy Blood
description: Reliquary containing the Blood of Christ brought by Thierry of Alsace.

name: Thierry of Alsace
description: Former Count of Flanders who brought the Holy Blood from the Holy Land.

name: Florum
description: Liege covenant in Ghent, founded by Jerbiton, using faerie-descended folk magicians to make cloth; supports a Lotharingian Tribunal.

name: Infelicitas
description: Lost covenant once suspected of causing the 1134 tidal wave.

name: Spider's Palace
description: Vassal of Florum on Florum's original site between Bruges and Ghent.

name: Requies Aeterna
description: A current covenant of Flanders and Picardy.

name: Flemish Cloth Fairs
description: Cycle of cloth-trade fairs in Lille, Mesen, Ypres, Torhout and Bruges.

name: Mesen
description: Flemish cloth fair town.

name: Torhout
description: Flemish cloth fair town.

name: Ghent
description: Largest city in Flanders, a center of cloth trade, home of Florum.

name: St. Amand
description: Apostle of Flanders who founded Ghent's monasteries and Christianized Antwerp.

name: Abbey of St. Bavo
description: Monastery in Ghent founded by St. Amand.

name: Baldwin II
description: Built a stone castle at Ghent.

name: Philip of Alsace
description: Count who rebuilt Ghent castle in 1180.

name: Church of St. Nicholas
description: Half-complete church in Ghent.

name: Graslei
description: Ghent's main docks.

name: Antwerp
description: Harbor city founded after Silvius Brabo defeated a giant.

name: Druon Antigon
description: A giant who plagued the Scheldt estuary cutting off hands; slain by Silvius Brabo.

name: Silvius Brabo
description: Roman soldier who defeated Druon Antigon.

name: Beguines
description: Movement of widows and unmarried women living in urban convents without vows.

name: St. Begga
description: 7th-century mother superior giving the Beguines their name.

name: Kattenfeest
description: Ypres ritual of hurling cats from the Cloth Hall belfry.

name: Ypres
description: Major Flemish cloth and linen city.

name: Cloth Hall of Ypres
description: Central hall where cats are kept and later hurled.

name: Yan den Houtkapper
description: Giant of Steenvoorde who made everlasting boots for Charlemagne.

name: Steenvoorde
description: Town parading a giant mannequin in armor.

name: Armor of the Giant of Steenvoorde
description: Huge armor from Charlemagne, possibly magical.

name: Everlasting Boots
description: Boots gifted to Charlemagne by Yan den Houtkapper.

name: Giant Blood
description: Virtue of giant ancestry.

name: Heuvelland
description: Flanders' uplands.

name: Tournai
description: Seat of Flanders' bishopric.

name: St. Piat
description: Converted Tournai.

name: Chilperic
description: Frankish king buried in Tournai.

name: Bavacum
description: Roman ruins at a seven-road junction with Magic aura 3 and journey-shortening roads.

name: Mercuralia
description: Roman festival of Mercury when all Bavacum roads work.

name: Reims
description: City with the Porte de Mars.

name: Pelagius of Jerbiton
description: Jerbiton magus who drew Florum's folk magicians into the House.

name: de Spinnens
description: Fictional family maintained by Florum.

name: The Farm
description: Florum's industrial complex south of Ghent.

name: Peripheral Code
description: Normandy Tribunal rulings; Florum's factory keeps wealth legal.
